style.text: MAY PASS BAL. 12 HCP VUL.
style.source: card (system summary); 'CAN PASS BAL 12 HCP VUL' on 1C
style.reading: with the rule of 20 only the 4-3-3-3 twelves then pass vulnerable; 'may' is a permission the rule makes always

style.text: RESPOND VERY LIGHT
style.reading: no field for the response minimum: responses start at 6 HCP

style.text: NV 4th seat overcall can be light
style.reading: no number given

style.text: LD is important. Wide Range. New suit NF
style.reading: lead-directing value is not placed

style.text: 1NT overcall: 15+-18, 2nd/4th LIVE. SOUND. System-On.
Re-opening 11-15
style.placed: comp.balancing_nt [11, 14] and comp.balancing_nt_major [11, 16] from the notes
style.reading: the card's one range, against the notes' two (11-14 vs 1m, 11-16 vs 1M); the notes are taken

style.text: Jump overcalls: PRE. Reopen: INTermediate
style.placed: comp.jump_overcall weak; balancing jumps intermediate (comp.balancing_jumps, default)

style.text: 1H/1S: Sound. Can be 4 NV in 3rd/4th
style.reading: no field for four-card major openings in 3rd/4th seat in a five-card system

style.text: 2D, 2H, 2S: WEAK TWO, Sound Vul; minimum six cards
style.reading: 'sound' read as the notes' 'good suit' (two of the top three)

style.text: Weak twos: Might open 1 in 3rd
style.placed: open.third_seat_min 10: a 10-11 count with five or more cards opens one in 3rd seat

style.text: 3C-3S: 7(6) cards, Sound Vul. 1st NV vs. V 'joke'
style.placed: open.three_level len 7; variants[1] vulnerable; variants[3] first seat favourable
style.reading: '(6)' (sometimes six cards) is placed only in first seat favourable

style.text: 4C, 4D: 7 cards, Aggressive NV. 4H, 4S: 7 cards, Sound, not too good
style.reading: no field separates a seven-card four-level opening from a seven-card three-level one; open.four_level stays at eight cards

style.text: 3NT: Solid minor. No A or K 1st-3rd
style.placed: open.three_nt gambling (solid seven-card minor, no outside ace or king)
style.reading: outside values in 4th seat are not placed

style.text: Takeout doubles: Sound. ELC. DBL of Preempt then new suit can be light.
style.reading: the light new suit after doubling a preempt is not placed

style.text: PSYCHICS: Rare
Open most balanced hands non-vul with 12 HCP, but could pass a bad one vul.
Open balanced 11 usually only NV and only if especially good (aces, tens).
style.reading: judgment by aces and tens

style.text: Unbalanced hands loosely follow the rule of 20, but use judgment based on honor location, spots, vul, and likely rebid problems.
If you have (say) stiff Q, don't count that for both 2 HCP and distribution!
style.reading: no predicate discounts a short honour

style.text: Might pass borderline hands if judgment is that they'll be easier to describe later.
style.reading: judgment

style.text: 3rd seat can open light, especially if you want that lead
Frequently respond light to opening bid, esp non vul
style.reading: no field for the response minimum

style.text: Routinely open 1N with 5-card major. 6-card m is possible, but never 'too good' a hand.
2-level opening should be 6-card suit in 1st/2nd.
'Good suit' = 2 of top 3. 'Good hand' = 8-10.
style.reading: Ogust's definitions; used for variants[1] and variants[2]

style.text: Fourth seat 2-level opening shows a maximum weak 2 bid - definitely less than a solid 1-level opening
3-level opening should be a 7-card suit with 4-6 playing tricks if non-vul, and 6-7 playing tricks if vul.
style.reading: playing tricks read as two of the top three honours

style.text: At imps, we play 1st seat FAVORABLE preempt can be VERY light - almost any hand with a 6-card suit would 'qualify'. At matchpoints, we do NOT do this.

Do not preempt if your hand is too good (even if partner is a PH) or has too many 'flaws', such as good playability in side majors (especially spades) or too much stuff in your short suits. Ideally, you should really want the lead in the suit you preempt in.
style.reading: the rest is judgment

style.text: Gambling 3NT: no outside A or K if 1st-3rd seat.
1N overcall is a good 15-18 HCP.
Fourth seat (sandwich) NT is 15-18 HCP.
style.reading: not compiled: action after both opponents have bid

style.text: Balancing 1N is 11-14 vs. 1m; 11-16 vs. 1M.
Balancing JUMP 2N overcall is 19-21 HCP.
style.reading: no balancing 2NT compiled

style.text: Double then 1N (or non-jump to 2N) by doubler is 18+-20 HCP
Double then jump to 2N by doubler is 21-22 HCP
style.reading: the doubler's rebid is not compiled

style.text: Balancing double then 1N (or non-jump to 2N) is 15-18 HCP (17-18 after 1M)
Overcalls are wide range - 7-17 HCP.
Balancing jump overcall is INTERMEDIATE - about an opening bid with 6-card suit
If advancer bids a suit at the 3-level, this shows values (about 7-10 HCP)
style.reading: action over two-level openings is not compiled

style.text: Balancing double can be a king light
style.source: notes (they open at the 2-level and at the 3-level)
style.reading: over two- and three-level openings: not compiled

style.text: Double is Take-out. Advancer should bid game with 9+ HCP
style.reading: not compiled

style.text: Double tends to be for T.O. Advancer usually needs a six-card suit or 5-5 to go to the 5-level

special doubles: (1NT-3NT) double asks for the weaker major; action double; stolen bid; Lightner; double of 3NT asks for our bid suit, or not their preempt suit
penalty pass of a redouble at the 3-level or higher, or of a solo bidder

leads: in partner's suit, high from xxx(x) if raised, xxS unless raised; vs NT the ace asks for an unblock or count, K from AK or KQ, Q from QJ or AQJ, J from J10 or KJ10, 10 from 109 or H109; 'K at 5+-level or sing.' vs suits; SSxx(x) vs NT

signals: vs suits, second priority on partner's lead 'HI = EVEN'; suit preference when dummy has a singleton; third priority on declarer's lead 'Informative'; 'SP vs. suits when no more tricks can be cashed or set up'; remainder count H/L = odd; split second-highest under declarer
